item.title: Night Terrors - Seeking Idea Critique
item.description: A child from an abusive home develops a dangerous anomaly as a self-defense mechanism - and she has no idea.
item.content:encoded:
I read, and reread the required reading, so I hope I didn't miss any crucial steps! I'm new to all of this.

Seeking Greenlights: Not currently, still in the very beginning stages.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch:

  • The core idea of this SCP is a child with C-PTSD from an unstable/abusive home life has developed anomalous properties, seemingly as a self-defense mechanism.
  • The child unknowingly manifests horrors that protect her in her sleep, but only in the event she has a nightmare.
  • The manifestation of these monsters will attack any other lifeform that comes within 3 meters of her as she slumbers.
  • The moment the child awakens from her nightmare, the monsters vanish, and the child is left with no inclination of what she has done - only that she's had a bad dream.

Central Narrative:
The child has been taken into Foundation care in an attempt to not only learn about her anomalies and why they seemingly manifested, and try to pinpoint what made these anomalies manifest in the first place.

Through trial and error the researchers assigned to her case begin to understand her condition, learn how to avoid potential manifestations of her monstrous protectors, and attempt to rehabilitate her in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The SCP within this story is just a normal little girl, who doesn't understand what is happening to her or why. She has no idea of her anomaly, only that she was "taken away" from her parents. This part I'm mildly struggling with. I feel like I have a good start here, I'm just not sure how to make this SCP stand out against thousands of others.

Additional Notes:
I have a good idea of what this SCP is, and what she can do, but I need a bit of help figuring out the specifics of her story. This is my first attempt at writing an SCP, and I want to make sure it's air tight before I even consider sending in a draft for serious critique. I have her containment procedures mapped out, and a bit of her description, but I'm unsure if what I have so far is even reasonable. I appreciate any assistance.

item.title: Alternative Classification System (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: A link to alternate Foundation database that uses different SCP classification methods.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (potentially -J if idea is decided to be too silly/meta by reviewers)

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch:
+ show block
– hide block

A connection on the internal Foundation database with unknown source that leads to a database of documented SCP Objects that is mostly identical to foundation's own, with key difference being that classification system used for SCP types is different. Connection severs itself and immedeately reinstates every 24 hours, connecting to a different alternative database. In addition to that, any attempt at documenting the SCP itself results in it changing its own classification to match whatever system is used in current connection.

Central Narrative:
+ show block
– hide block

The connection is direct and two-way, but read-only veiw into a tiny glimpse of life of Foundation in alternate reality. Due to nature of the SCP all realities remain the same in terms of amount of knowledge on SCPs themselves and state of foundation, with extremely rare exceptions. However, differences in things unrelated to SCPs themselves are fairly common, if hard to find due to nature of the materials being accessed. In addition, all the access restrictions are still perfectly functional, so researcher in charge of the SCP cannot access any particularly classified one without direct permission. Through continuous observation, Foundation also finds very minor ways to enchance its performance, though again, in fields unrelated to the handling or finding SCPs themselves.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
+ show block
– hide block

Primarily, the article would be a list of various alternative systems of classification recorded, ranging from reasonable to completely absurd to downright esoteric. Regular notes about differences that aren't the system itself would also allow it to not be excessively repetitive.

Additional Notes:
+ show block
– hide block

The focus will mostly be lighthearted moreso than comedic, if it is approved as regular article. Main inspiration for the article has been growth of use of esoteric SCP Classes in recent articles, and its meant to be a light little meta reference to that, while still being reasonable as a standalone thing.

item.title: SCP Concept: The Dream Zombies (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: Weird after-affects.
item.content:encoded:
A child's bed that makes people who sleep in it dream of zombies. Weird after-affects.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking-Greenlights: Yes

Page-Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page-Layout: Default SCP-Layout

Elevator-Pitch:

SCP-XXXX is a small patterned child's bed that emits a comforting attraction-aura of childhood and nostalgia. The bed makes any entity that sleeps in it have nightmares of green-glowing zombies attempting to eat their stomach. In dreams, people "get out of bed" in their current/old household (sometimes-combined).

After sleeping in the SCP, the user will have these nightmares every-time they go to sleep anywhere.
When having nightmares, people suddenly wake up in a panicked-state, which causes sleep deprivation. Some experience PTSD.

If multiple people feel the attraction of the SCP, all shall get aggressive at one-another and fight until one remains/all die. Aura-attraction to SCP is instant ONLY in a 10-feet radius to the SCP, and ONLY goes away for 9-to-15-minutes after awakening from it.

+ READ MORE
- READ LESS

Central-Narrative:

SCP-XXXX was found by Field-Agent, Chris, in Florida when investigating multiple reports of "eeriness" of an abandoned hospital from locals. Agent-C, under SCPs attraction-affect, realized the affect and called for backup. Three other Field-Agents arrived (with recording hardware) and found Agent-C sleeping in the SCP. All agents felt the affect of SCP, ending with a fight between the four agents where Agent-K killed all three other agents with a pistol and slept in the SCP.

Mobile Task Force Psi-7 was called in by Agent-K after waking up and leaving, which all twenty MTF were not able to contain the SCP due its attraction force. MTF member, Cadet-F, survived bloodshed and reported the incident after sleeping.

Agent-K and Cadet-F were taken into investigation with recorded evidence/interviews of what occurred.
Both were carefully watched over in-study by research staff, where Foundation realized consistent nightmares.
Both were given amnesics and therapy all which only helped endurance with the-nightmares and trauma. (SCP-500-use blocked by 05-council for scarcity-issues)

Agent-K was also questioned in later dates/interviews to describe any further issues he experienced (such as nightmares).

The SCP is left in the abandoned-building, guarded by 10 undercover guards looking like U.S-police to ensure locals don't enter.
Only researchers/needed-personnel are allowed inside.

D-Class studies/interviews/experiments and small-animal research confirmed SCP's affects like nightmares, aura-attraction, PTSD, and sleep deprivation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

Based on real nightmares I had as a kid after playing the game "Nicktoons Unite!".

Unlike other Bed-SCPs, it anomaly/nightmares "sticks" to its users.

Story is short-&-sweet.

Additional-Notes: (Ask for more detailed-explanations)

item.title: Greenlight request: Tattooed hydraulic press
item.description: [thread locked, repeat]
item.content:encoded:
A press with patches of tattooed skin on it and a dark story behind it

Thread summary moved to the main post as the thread is now locked.

Seeking Greenlight: Yes
Page type: SCP Article

First of all sorry for my repost. I didn't get any greenlights or the amount of feedback I had hoped for. Also I'm new to the wiki so I don't know the proper channels.

The SCP is already written by me and is currently residing in my sandbox until I get enough greenlights to get the SCP reviewed.

Elevator pitch:
SCP-XXXX is a hydraulic press which from a first glance doesn’t seem that weird. It seems like just the ordinary hydraulic press located in different factories across the world. But upon further notice, you see that it contains several patches of skin with tattoos on them. To make things even weirder you notice that the skin doesn't match a specific skin tone (it differs from white to black skin tones). You come closer to the press and you're fascinated by the different tattoos displayed on its metalic frame. But then all the sudden…….

+ show block
– hide block

The machine transforms into a metalic cat like being with several blades coming from its body. The being moves closer at a fast speed and then all of the sudden one of its blades rips the tattooed flesh from your body with surgeon like skills. As you bleed your vision becomes blur. It gets blurrier and blurrier and just before you pass out, you see the being transform back into the hydraulic press. You see it pulvarize the flesh it took and then all the sudden your tattoo seems to appear on its metalic frame. Suddenly everything is dark and you're no more. But a part of you is now part of SCP-XXXX.

Central narrative:
A part of the SCP file is dedicated to the retrieval of SCP-XXXX. One of the researchers of SCP-XXXX interviews Agent Ford who helped to retrieve the SCP. During this interview we learn about the circumstances in which SCP-XXXX has been found and contained.
Example:
In 1988 several people went missing from a small town named Lockhart in Texas. A anonymous phone call from a women got the police to believe that the missing people were held at the Johnson & son factory in town. After some searching the officers and a foundation agent named Ford found a pile of dead bodies, their tattooed flesh ripped from their bodies. And next to it SCP-XXXX (the tattooed hydraulic press).

After the retrieval of SCP-XXXX the reader gets to read about research performed on SCP-XXXX. The reader learns about the nature of SCP-XXXX’s anomylous abilities. For example: SCP-XXXX has two modes of existence. It has its hydraulic press body which have several tattooed flesh patches on its frame, and it also has a secondary body, which is a cat like being into which the tattooed press transforms.

The research leads to several incidents and eventually to adjustments to the special containment procedures performed. While research is also starting to search for a way to use SCP-XXXX for the retrieval of other SCP's.

item.title: Seeking greenlight : Miserable man stuck in a movie
item.description: A drunk forgetful man stuck in a movie because he deserved it
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional.

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout.

Elevator Pitch: A broken man is stuck in his own hell, a 86 minute movie starring him, but something else is under the surface.

+ Central Narrative:
- Hide Central Narrative:

Bryce Cromwell was an average man, he never saw anything supernatural and worked a normal 9 to 5. But one day, he had been diagnosed with Alzheimer's and this changed his world forever. Words began to slip from his mind, things that should be there just weren't, and the only thing that forever was there was alcohol. And so he drank, he drank his worries, his mind away. He drank so much he didn't even remember his daughter or his wife, the only things that brought joy into this dark world. One night he drank too much, so much he forgot the pain of the crash, the crash that took his wife and daughter. After he woke up he was more sober than usual and could remember everything except the crash, he was horrified to see his wife and daughter's dead body in the trunk of his car. He wept for hours until he felt a presence behind him. A woman appeared, what he didn't know was that the woman was the titan Mnemosyne, the titan of memories. She proclaimed his sins and cursed him with the worst of fates, and so he was stuck in a cassette tape which held a 86 minute movie which when played would split his mind apart, one side when never played with his memories intact yet no concept of time, and his awake half which couldn't remember yet knew what time was. And so he was stuck for years like that until the foundation found him.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fear of what is inescapable, forgetting all that you learned and just how destructive our choices and what we can't control truly are.

Additional Notes: Second SCP, give me all you got.

item.title: Seeking Greenlights: My Eyes are Up Here
item.description: An anomaly on a researcher's chest that causes memory loss
item.content:encoded:
An anomaly on a researcher's chest that causes memory loss, change in eye color, or painful, permanent blindness depending on the duration of time one spends staring at it.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy/Horror(?)

Elevator Pitch: SCP researchers discover that after staring at the chest area of one of their female co-workers for over ten seconds, the word "M I N E" seems to appear on it etched in blood, changing the observer's eye color to an alarming shade of magenta and causing blindness if they continue staring.

Central Narrative: People frequently wondered why Dr. Jenna Lopez never seemed to mind that Dr. Briggs kept staring at her chest. Strangely, if anyone mentioned his ogling, both doctors would deny that he was ever looking, both appearing confused by the suggestion that such an event had ever occurred, until the events of August 9th, 2020. That day, at lunch in the cafeteria, Dr. Briggs was "enjoying the view", when suddenly, he started screaming.

+ show block
– hide block

Co-workers turned to him, only to find that his irises had turned a viciously-bright shade of magenta. He, in a panicked frenzy, claimed that this was the first time he had ever looked at her chest, then vehemently insisted that he'd seen the word "M I N E" appear on her as if carved into the exposed skin. Other researchers, including Dr. Lopez herself, glanced down, only to see nothing of the sort. Briggs tried to insist again, continuing to look at her as the security team was called, only for him to start screaming again, this time out of intense pain rather than shock. Briggs then went fully blind. Lopez was temporarily confined, and tests started being performed.

Note: Lopez seems to completely lack control or intention regarding these effects, such that SCP-XXXX is identified as solely her chest, rather than the woman herself.

Containment: Since only exposed skin seems to cause the effects described, Lopez is allowed to roam free so long as she continues to wear clothing that covers her bosom (as well as an SCP-commissioned undergarment to prevent the effects from seeping through non-opaque fabrics). The classification is, for the time being, safe.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: First, the humor and righteousness of an SCP that punishes perverts who stare at this poor woman's chest. Second, the idea and potential ethical debate of an SCP attached to a non-SCP human person.

A fir tree plantation that is actually the place where the hunter tracks down and kills trespassers. Once someone gets in they are unable to leave and now they’re stuck in the plantation until the hunter murders them or lets his dogs get there first.

Central Narrative
- The site is noted by the foundation but not much is done to properly contain/research into it since the hunter was never seen before (and lack of funds). People thought that those who were never seen again simply got lost in the site due to it being infinite.
- They do yearly checks but keep CCTV around the site and rope off any possible entrances and/or holes in the fences. In 2012, a research team moves down to the surrounding area because of sufficient funding to finally perform studies on the plantation.
- A few days later they call down the Foundation’s militia because a body has turned up by the fence with lacerations caused by a large hound covering their legs and a bullet wound to the back and head. The SCP is properly contained from then with armed guards and appropriate measures. They send in test dummies from time to time equipped with cameras to see if they can capture any footage of this hunter.
- All that comes back is unusable audio but near-perfect footage of the plantation morphing around the subjects, displacing them and sending them into the ‘dimension’ of the hunter, his own personal playground for unsuspecting trespassers.
- They stop sending in dummies since they all end up getting killed so now most of the team’s time is spent taking samples carefully.

item.title: Hephaestus - SCP Concept
item.description: An SCP describing a wildfire which is not extinguishable.
item.content:encoded:
Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Typical Layout (SC Procedures, Description, Addenda)

Genre: No specific genre

Elevator Pitch: The SCP (Preferably SCP-5766) is a wildfire located in Northern Norway started in late April of 2010 approximately 0.43 square kilometres in area. The SCP lacks the ability of being extinguished at least for long-term periods.

Central Narrative: SCP was started in late April of 2010 at 2:00 PM during a lightning storm that had killed over 200 separate creatures including foxes, wolves, reindeer, and puffins. SCP was presumably started when a lightning strike lit several coniferous trees affected by dry-rot.

SCP was discovered by a hiker during a hike in Northern Norway. At 4pm, he noticed a large quantity of soot and smoke in the trees, a noticeable change in visibility of the area and an increased air temperature. He followed what he presumed where the smoke originated from, and unknowingly discovered SCP while the large volume of smoke in the area, however he never noticed the presence of SCP.

The Foundation was first notified of SCP from the Norwegian Government when a collection of meteorologists and climatologists noticed an unusual quantity of smoke coming from the region of the SCP’s presence. The Foundation investigated and put containment of the object into effect.

SCP began forming a local greenhouse effect across its nearby regions on the 13th of September 2012, through immense emission of Carbon Dioxide and Water Vapour, causing intense heat during the day and night hours in the region.

Attention-Grabber: This SCP is the first SCP mainly focused on wildfires.

Addenda:

  • Hephaestus is the God of Fire in Greek Mythology.

item.title: SCP Concept: Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is an anomalous event in a gas station, where if an individual looks at the bathroom's mirror for enough time they will be controlled and later killed by their reflection.

Central Narrative: An SCP Foundation Researcher is driving in his car to his house, he suddenly sees a gas station and stops there to wash his face. He enters the bathroom and begins realizing this gas station was never here before, hence why he didn't recognize it. As he was washing his face, the Researcher began looking intently at the mirror and started scratching his arm uncontrollably, grabbed his hair and breathed heavily, showing signs of paranoia, then suddenly began acting against his own will and followed his reflection's movement. After a bit, the reflection smiled and grabbed a hammer, so did the Researcher, they both swung the hammer towards the mirror, shattering it, and the Staff member dropped dead in the bathroom with multiple cuts around his body. show
Hide

The area around the anomaly isn't alien in nature, as it is very similar to our own universe.
The body, however, seems to send signals that are telepathic in nature. However, the only thing the foundation was able to decipher said, "Please help."

Central Narrative: After a site was built around the SCP, explorations by MTF agents were made into the factory

Show
Hide

In the first exploration log, they find the woman and discover it's not the factory that has been the anomalous one (although it does have some slight anomalous properties itself), it was her. They then find a pinboard with a paper reading "Bring your kid to work day!" with a date on it, (we saw how that went). An unlocked laptop with an OS similar to windows. The owner of the laptop is named Janis Phenix, who is the anomaly. A document is open on the laptop, its Janis' journal, and she writes about how she was embarrassed to be one of the small group that actually participated in "bring your kid to work day" but says it doesn't matter because her boss told her to come to something called "The Creator Room," and it's making her anxious all day for some reason. The foundation unable to access the previous days of the journal, but was able to download it for some reason.
In the second exploration log, an MTF was sent to recover as much information as they could. They found documents on every employee, and they find out that Janis was an anomalous artist and crafter (NOT part of AWCY?) who made the teddy bear her son was holding. Another thing they find is a map of the factory, and find that the underground parts are bigger than the above ground.
Back at control, the files from the laptop are sent. In the previous pages of the journal, Janis was promoted to work on something called "Project Dramaturgy," commissioned by a group called The LUC agency (this should be a major clue, if not tell me), they didn't know what exactly what they were creating or what it would be used for, but they could care less as they had a budget bigger than anything they would ever get. They were told to make an anomalous human out of the materials they had given them, they worked on it for a while and were near finished. The journal ends with the journal entry of her being embarrassed about being one of the small group that actually brought their kids.
In the third exploration log, the team is sent to the lower floors, where they find "anomaly creators." In the room Janis' boss asked her to be in, the creator room, they find a large containment cell (that was most likely breached) and a sheaf of papers describing the experiment. Long story short the LUC commissioned the factory, and they experiment on LUC agency (the SCP foundation of their universe) D-class and attempted to make a human superweapon, everything was fine until Janis' son brought his anomalous teddy bear and it triggered a chain reaction that caused the breach (as stated before in the journal, she made the teddy bear while she wasn't experienced much with anomalies herself). The SCP foundation theorizes that every employee in the factory also experienced what Janis did and was moved to a separate universe.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For readers into SCP articles with plenty of exploration logs and mystery to solve, this can be a good article for them

item.title: SCP: The Tooth Jar (seeking greenlights)

Elevator Pitch:

  • SCP-XXXX is an ordinary looking empty glass jar
  • If a human subject is eating a meal within a short distance radius around SCP-XXXX, teeth will appear inside the food
  • Putting these teeth inside the jar will transmute them into radioactive coins
+ Show more
- Show less

Central Narrative:

SCP-XXXX is a ordinary looking glass jar that can be opened or closed with a metallic lid. Manufacturing codes engraved at the bottom of SCP-XXXX suggest it originally was a jar of Dijon mustard.

Eating solid food within a 20 meter radius around SCP-XXXX will have the following effect occur: after chewing four to five times, the subject will bite on a small human tooth, that was not initially present in the food. This tooth, called SCP-XXXX-1, matches the DNA of the subject that bit on it, although no loss of tooth is observed on the subject.

This phenomenon can be repeated. An instance of SPC-XXXX-1 will appear in the consumed food every four to five mastications, and this will always result in the subject biting onto it, leading to possible mouth injuries if unprepared.
Every time an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 is created, its mass is substracted from the subject's bone mass. Excessive repetition of the phenomenon on the same subject will result in the onset of bone-related diseases, such as osteoporosis.

Placing instances of SCP-XXXX-1 into SCP-XXXX, closing it with the lid, and breaking all visual contact with it allow for the transmutation event to take place instantly.
The transmutation event can occur only if no human person or camera has a visual contact with SCP-XXXX. The transmutation effectively replaces all instances of SCP-XXXX-1 with coins, referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-2 look identical to coins of the French Franc currency. Composition and engravings on the surface matches that of regular coins melted in 1982.
All instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are highly radioactive, averaging 80 μSv/h, warranting their rapid disposal.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Have you ever bitten on your own dislodged tooth while eating, when you were a child? It's not the most pleasant of sensations. This SCP also twists the tale of the tooth fairy in a SCP-esque fashion.

item.title: {Seeking Greenlight} The Devil You Know
item.description: Beats the Devil you don't.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Weird

Elevator Pitch: Anyone who directly observes subject through sight or sound is suddenly and unwaveringly convinced the source is from a long-forgotten friend or lover they remember fondly, regardless whether said witnesses has any actual history with subject. The subject's evocative aura actively alters or erases previous experiences in their minds to replace them with its own interpretations, leading many victims to become near obsessed with the entity after extended periods. Subject has potential to teleport near anyone previously exposed to its anomalous presence, manifesting instantaneously around corners or behind doors.

+ Negating Other Mind-Affecting Anomalies
- Hide

The most notable and bizarre feature to this process, however, is that continued exposure to the subject's anomalous presence can completely eliminate any pre-existing mental manipulative affects placed upon any human’s mind. For example, if another anomalous effect from another SCP-recorded creature infects their victim's mind with permanent delusions or extreme abnormal behavior, prolonged and repeated exposure to this subject's presence through conversation can remedy these effects. Required intervals of exposure necessary to perform this ranges from days to years, depending on how powerful said previous mental afflictions were.

Central Narrative: The entity was borne out of an unknown man’s own sacrifice to ritualistically create something from the collective unconscious of humanity; unfortunately considered a failure, as a tether connected human consciousness remains attached. Subject finds mild entertainment in playing with the strings of human minds, observing them as charming yet fickle and simplistic instruments of manipulation. Anomalous effects are second-nature and hardly intentional, though also has an intuitive understanding to read human emotions with 100% accuracy from its direct connection to human consciousness that was not severed during its creation. It rarely expresses any strong emotions, however grows more compelled to assist the foundation in efforts to either understand or combat other mind-affecting anomalies, considering them a threat or challenge to its domain.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature can be dangerous due to its addictive aura and teleportative capabilities, but the utilization of said anomalous properties to counteract active influence of other mind-affecting SCP creatures can be an invaluable asset.

item.title: First SCP.
item.description: A polish immigrant who runs a butchershop and deli is secretly a Sarkite who uses his powers to make the best meat around.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A well liked butcher in the area turns out to be empowered by the power of the flesh to produce the best cuts.

Central Narrative: A story of a Polish sarkite who flees his community during the chaos at the end of WWI and emigrates to America for a normal life. He finds work running a butcher shop and deli. He's able to do this by cloning beef and pork and manipulating it to be the best possible cut of meat to work with. This causes him to be popular and wealthy as he doesn't need to keep buying new meat. It does cause people to spread rumors about mob ties as he sometimes talks to scary looking men who aren't from the area. He dies and tells his son to not get involved in sarkicism, that the UIU and Foundation will deal with any problems about it, and that he' a good enough butcher to not need flesh warping powers.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Turns out the butcher who everyone thinks has mob ties and might be a cannibal is actually neither. Though the truth isn't all that comforting

Additional Notes: This is my second idea for my first SCP. The basic feed back from my first try a few weeks ago basically boiled down to it being too similar to another SCP and not very narrative. So I put that idea on the back burner and came up with something I thought would be more narrative.

item.title: Snatcher Slug (Seeking Critique)
item.description: My first SCP, currently seeking critique and maybe a greenlight, but not quite yet.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Not yet

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an SCP that can attach itself to a host, designated SCP-XXXX-1, in the form of a small slug that slowly feeds off of its host until the host is completely alone from anyone else and is isolated somewhere where it can not be detected killing them. It then pumps a potent, instantly acting neurotoxin into their bloodstream and assimilates as them, eating them for nutrition. SCP-XXXX then goes around as SCP-XXXX-1, designated as -2 from that point. It releases more small instances of SCP-XXXX that repeat the process, and after a period of two years, -2 dies. SCP-XXXX can infect any sufficiently complex organism, and inherits all abilities of that organism. It has been observed assimilating with dogs, cats, and even a juvenile Kokomo dragon. A definite way to detect -2 is to take a Copper or Gold wire heated to at least 15° Celsius and submerge it lightly in a blood sample of -2. When the wire touches the blood, it jumps away. Containing it is somewhat difficult, as it can assimilate into anyone and can not be killed with regular firearms. Instead, to permanently destroy or severely incapacitate it requires using incendiary weaponry. It can survive in pretty much any environment, but to contain it, there is a small room, where over the course of a day, 12 gallons of pig's blood is pumped in for XXXX. The room has 14 different cameras with overlapping sight lines. Past that room is an airlock where there are flamethrower countermeasures installed and infrared scanners to detect the abnormally high body temperature of XXXX.

Central Narrative: A Foundation Research team of twelve researchers are moving to investigate an odd increase in the electromagnetic pulses emanating from the South Pole. They find a large asteroid buried under some ice that seems to have been there for at least 120.000 years, unearthed by melting ice. The team takes back a large canister filled with slugs back to Site-118 for study, but the organisms assimilate with them and manage to destroy the base. MTF Upsilon-6 "Cold Shoulder" (I couldn't find an MTF Squadron with the description I needed so I made one up) attempts to retrieve the scientists, unknowingly bringing back instances of -2 to Site-29, which spreads the infection of XXXX. It is recaptured and contained at Site-29, where the slugs are contained.

item.title: People Seeds
item.description: Inspired by the thought experiment by Judith Jarvis Johnson
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A plant that unpredictably grows on unmarked or secluded graves. The plant then releases seeds that drift through the air and land in a new place. The plant matures into a baby with the exact genetic makeup of the deceased.

Narrative: The plant begins to grow on a site where D-class and other Foundation bodies are disposed of, resurrecting and scattering hundreds of them across the nation. The article then follows the efforts of the Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed (most of whom have reintegrated into society), robbing them of their second chance. Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A heart-wrenching story of love, loss, reanimation, and what happens when a second chance at life isn't enough.

Sorrow for her fallen children, and sorrow for sending her children to die in who knows how many wars that they never won. So she packed her things and left the mainland, retreating to an island. Many, many years later, the foundation responds to a radio signal from a battleship claiming that they were being attacked by an enormous spider. It's revealed that she created this spider as a guardian for her personal island that she sends out if she senses that people with bad intentions are coming to her island. item.title: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification
item.description: Short tale expansion for SCP-5118.
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/deathbygin-2

A short tale for my authored article SCP-5118.

Spoiler / Explanation
Minimize

As Dr. Atmos gather information from Dr. Williams, it's implied that SCP-5118 is actually a dog who is a reality bender, turned human, and turned back into a dog when about to be captured. Evidence to support this includes:

  • SCP-5118 did not act like most other reality benders do when discovering they have powers (usually by hiding them from others).
  • SCP-5118 manifests chocolate, grapes, and soda - all things a dog cannot eat.
  • SCP-5118 appeared to be smiling while being chased.
  • SCP-5118 does not attempt to breach containment because it's current living situation is already ideal (it gets a bed, new toys, guaranteed food and water, and socializes with staff daily when they provide it with food).
  • Using it's powers while in containment would risk exposing itself. Since it's implied that it's "original form" is already a dog, the scans / tests from the SCP article would show nothing.

I wanted to write this tale to add a twist to the article without making this the clear-cut canon. Please let me know what you think.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that the SCPs are based on Irish fairies, who are (in short) tricksters who manipulate humans in various ways. Whether that be by manipulating their mind to go crazy or manipulating their body to disform them. Fairies were blamed for various things in medieval Ireland, some of those include stuff like schizophrenia or disabilities being 'curses' from fairies. The SCP will differ from generic fairies by being inherently malevolent when the original fairies are not.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: After various missing person reports, and the discovery of a body missing a symmetrical hole in their chest, the Foundation investigate a forest in Ireland. While investigating, one of the team starts hearing voices telling them to kill their teammates and to 'come to the festival' upon telling the team of this the MTF, assuming the SCP has something to do with this, detain and amnestisize the teammate. They leave one MTF to bring the affected teammate out of the forest to safety and continue. After a bit, the MTF see various colorful lights in the distance, and they all begin to hear voices telling them to 'come to the festival'. At this point, the MTF stop broadcasting their video and we are left with only their audio. The captain, who appears to be the least affected, describes what's happening while the others start going mad. Eventually, the captain attempts to flee the situation at which various etheral screaming can be heard before he goes offline.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Well I tried my best to make sure it leaves a lot of questions, and the fact that it's a twist on what is normally considered cute or harmless is pretty interesting.

Additional Notes: I don't know how I feel about the narrative (which is why I'm not seeking a greenlight yet), so I would like critisicm to be focused on that.
